# Preface {.unnumbered}

## Purpose

This guide explains how to run Arma 3 on a Linux computer. It also covers the installation of two radio communication plugins – ACRE2 and TFAR – which many Arma 3 communities use. Both plugins need setup that the base game does not.

Linux cannot run Windows games natively. Valve's Proton compatibility layer bridges this gap. Proton translates Windows instructions into Linux equivalents at runtime. The process is largely transparent once configured.

The guide is written for readers with basic Linux terminal experience. Each step is explained in full. Where a command must be typed, the exact command is shown in a code block. Read each section before executing any command.

## Scope

This guide covers:

- System preparation and dependency installation.
- Steam and Proton configuration.
- Arma 3 download and initial launch.
- The Arma3Helper script and its use.
- TeamSpeak 3 (Windows version) installation inside Proton.
- ACRE2 plugin installation and configuration.
- TFAR plugin installation and configuration.
- Troubleshooting common problems.
- Performance optimisation.

This guide does not cover:

- Arma 3 server administration.
- Mod development.
- Windows or macOS systems.

## Fork and Purpose

This repository is a community-maintained fork of the original `armaonlinux` project. It was developed by members of our milsim community to provide enhanced documentation, improved installation scripts, and better support for custom configurations.

While created to streamline the onboarding process for our own members, we have made this public to support the wider Arma on Linux/Unix community. Our goal is to provide a full, professional resource that allows anyone, regardless of experience level, to successfully play Arma 3 on Linux.

\newpage

# Chapter 1 – Understanding the Technology

## What Is Proton?

Proton is a compatibility layer developed by Valve. It allows Linux users to run Windows games through Steam. Proton is built on top of Wine, an open-source Windows compatibility project. Valve adds significant improvements to Wine, including better graphics performance and game-specific fixes.

Each game running under Proton has its own isolated Windows environment. This is called a **Wine prefix** or **compatdata** directory. The prefix contains a virtual Windows file system. Changes made inside one prefix do not affect others or the host Linux system.

Arma 3's Wine prefix is stored at:

```
<SteamLibrary>/steamapps/compatdata/107410/
```

The number `107410` is Arma 3's Steam Application ID. This number is used throughout the guide and in configuration files.

## What Is ACRE2?

ACRE2 stands for Advanced Combat Radio Environment 2. It is an Arma 3 mod that simulates realistic military radio communication. When active, players hear radio traffic through their headset as though using a real radio. Sound quality, distance, and terrain all affect communication.

ACRE2 requires a TeamSpeak 3 plugin to function. The plugin must run inside the same Wine prefix as Arma 3. It cannot use the native Linux version of TeamSpeak.

ACRE2 depends on CBA_A3 (Community Base Addons for Arma 3). This mod must also be active for ACRE2 to work. Both are available on the Steam Workshop.

## What Is TFAR?

TFAR stands for Task Force Arrowhead Radio. Like ACRE2, it is an Arma 3 mod that simulates radio communication through TeamSpeak 3. TFAR is widely used by European Arma communities.

TFAR also requires a TeamSpeak 3 plugin. Unlike ACRE2, TFAR does not install its plugin automatically. The Arma3Helper script installs it with a single command, described in Chapter 9.

ACRE2 and TFAR serve the same purpose but are incompatible with each other. A community uses one or the other. Check with your unit before installing either.

## Why Not Use Native Linux TeamSpeak?

The ACRE2 and TFAR plugins are compiled for Windows. They cannot load into the native Linux TeamSpeak client. The only supported approach is to run the Windows version of TeamSpeak 3 inside Arma's Wine prefix. The Arma3Helper script automates this.

# Chapter 2 – Prerequisites and System Preparation

## Hardware and Software Requirements

The following are required before starting:

- A 64-bit Linux installation (any modern distribution).
- A Steam account with Arma 3 purchased.
- An internet connection for downloads.
- Approximately 50 GB of free disk space for the game.

The following software must be present before proceeding. Most distributions include these by default. Install any that are missing using your package manager.

- `bash` (version 4 or newer).
- `curl` (used by the Arma3Helper script for updates).
- GPU drivers appropriate for your hardware. Keep them up to date.
- `winetricks` or `protontricks` (used by the script to install DirectX and audio libraries into Arma's prefix).

## Enabling 32-bit Support (Multilib)

Steam uses 32-bit components internally. Audio support under Proton also requires 32-bit libraries. You must enable 32-bit package support on your distribution before installing GStreamer and related packages.

### Arch Linux

Edit the Pacman configuration file:

``` bash
sudo nano /etc/pacman.conf
```

Find the following two lines. They will be commented out with a `#` character at the start:

```
#[multilib]
#Include = /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist
```

Remove the `#` from both lines so they read:

```
[multilib]
Include = /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist
```

Save the file and update the package database:

``` bash
sudo pacman -Sy
```

### Debian and Ubuntu

Enable 32-bit package support with:

``` bash
sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386
sudo apt update
```

### Fedora

Fedora supports 32-bit packages through its standard repositories. No additional configuration is needed.

## Installing GStreamer

Arma 3 uses GStreamer to handle audio. Proton requires both the 64-bit and 32-bit versions. Install them for your distribution:

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: {.panel-tabset}

### Arch Linux
``` bash
sudo pacman -S gstreamer gst-plugins-base gst-plugins-good \
lib32-gstreamer lib32-gst-plugins-base lib32-gst-plugins-good
```

### Debian/Ubuntu
``` bash
sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-tools gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
gstreamer1.0-tools:i386 gstreamer1.0-plugins-base:i386 \
gstreamer1.0-plugins-good:i386
```

### Fedora
``` bash
sudo dnf install gstreamer1 gstreamer1-plugins-base \
gstreamer1-plugins-good \
gstreamer1.i686 gstreamer1-plugins-base.i686 \
gstreamer1-plugins-good.i686
```
:::
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Arch Linux**
``` bash
sudo pacman -S gstreamer gst-plugins-base gst-plugins-good \
lib32-gstreamer lib32-gst-plugins-base lib32-gst-plugins-good
```

**Debian/Ubuntu**
``` bash
sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-tools gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
gstreamer1.0-tools:i386 gstreamer1.0-plugins-base:i386 \
gstreamer1.0-plugins-good:i386
```

**Fedora**
``` bash
sudo dnf install gstreamer1 gstreamer1-plugins-base \
gstreamer1-plugins-good \
gstreamer1.i686 gstreamer1-plugins-base.i686 \
gstreamer1-plugins-good.i686
```
:::
## Resolving Startup Crashes

If Arma 3 crashes on startup, it is often due to outdated GPU drivers or missing Vulkan libraries. To resolve these issues:

- **Update GPU Drivers:** Keep your system's graphics drivers up to date. For AMD and Intel users, this means keeping your **Mesa** drivers current. NVIDIA users should install the latest proprietary drivers.
- **Install Vulkan Libraries:** Install the Vulkan support packages your distribution needs (for example `vulkan-tools`, `mesa-vulkan-drivers`).
- **Clear Shader Cache:** If the game crashes after previously working, the local shader cache may be corrupted. You can safely clear this by deleting the contents of the shader cache directory for Arma 3 (Steam App ID 107410):
``` bash
rm -rf ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/shadercache/107410/*
```
- **Verify Proton:** If issues persist, use Steam's 'Verify Integrity of Game Files' feature.


## Installing winetricks or protontricks

The Arma3Helper script uses either `winetricks` or `protontricks` to install Windows components into Arma's Wine prefix. At least one must be installed.

`protontricks` is generally preferred for Steam games because it correctly identifies the game's prefix automatically. Install whichever your distribution provides. Both can coexist without conflict.

### Arch Linux

``` bash
# Install protontricks from AUR using your preferred AUR helper:
yay -S protontricks

# Or install winetricks:
sudo pacman -S winetricks
```

### Debian and Ubuntu

``` bash
sudo apt install winetricks

# protontricks can be installed via pip:
pip install protontricks --break-system-packages
```

### Fedora
``` bash
sudo dnf install winetricks
```

# Chapter 3 – Steam and Proton Configuration

## Installing Steam

If Steam is not already installed, install it from your distribution's package manager. Install the official Steam package, not a third-party wrapper.

``` bash
# Arch Linux:
sudo pacman -S steam

# Debian/Ubuntu:
sudo apt install steam

# Fedora (from RPM Fusion repository):
sudo dnf install steam
```

Launch Steam and log into your account before continuing.

## Enabling Steam Play for All Titles

Steam Play is Valve's branding for Proton compatibility. It must be enabled for games that do not have a native Linux version.

Open Steam. Click **Steam** in the top menu bar, then click **Settings**. In the settings window, scroll to **Steam Play** in the left column.

Enable both of the following:

- **Enable Steam Play for supported titles**
- **Enable Steam Play for all other titles**

In the dropdown labelled **Run other titles with**, select the latest stable Proton version available. Do not select **Proton Experimental** – it receives frequent changes and may introduce instability.

Click **OK** and restart Steam when prompted.

## Setting a Proton Version Specifically for Arma 3

The global Steam Play setting applies Proton to all games. Arma 3 also needs a version pinned specifically for it. This keeps Arma on a known good version regardless of the global default.

Right-click on Arma 3 in your Steam library. Click **Properties**.

Navigate to the **Compatibility** tab. Enable the checkbox labelled **Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool**.

Select the same Proton version you selected above. Close the Properties window.

Make a note of the Proton version you selected. Arma3Helper normally detects the Proton version from the prefix automatically. You only need to set it manually in the config file if auto-detection fails.

## Adding Arma 3 Launch Options

Arma 3 can be launched with the official launcher or with the `-nolauncher` flag to bypass it. The Arma 3 Unix Launcher (described in Chapter 4) is the recommended approach. If you intend to use the `-nolauncher` flag, add it here.

In Arma 3's Steam Properties, go to the **General** tab. In the **Launch Options** field, add:

```
%command% -nolauncher
```

The `-nolauncher` flag skips the official Bohemia Interactive launcher. This is optional but speeds up startup. The Arma 3 Unix Launcher is a superior replacement when managing mods.

## Understanding Custom Proton Builds (GE-Proton)

Community-built Proton versions exist alongside the official ones. The most common is **GE-Proton** (Glorious Eggroll Proton). GE-Proton includes patches and fixes not yet in official Proton.

For most users, official Proton is enough for Arma 3. GE-Proton is worth trying if you encounter specific issues that official Proton does not resolve.

Custom Proton builds are installed into:

```
~/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d/
```

Tools such as **ProtonUp-Qt** and **ProtonPlus** simplify the installation of GE-Proton. They are available in most distribution repositories and on Flathub.

Once a custom build is installed, you can select it in Steam under the **Compatibility** tab for Arma 3. The Arma3Helper script can also use it. Run `./Arma3Helper.sh listproton` to see all installed versions.

\newpage

# Chapter 4 – Installing Arma 3

## Before You Download

Complete all steps in Chapters 2 and 3 before downloading Arma 3. The Proton version must be set before the first download. Changing it afterwards requires reinstalling the game.

If you have Arma 3 on an external drive or a secondary Steam library, Steam will detect this automatically. The Arma3Helper script also handles external library paths without manual configuration.

## Downloading and First Launch

In your Steam library, click on Arma 3 and start the download. Allow the download to complete fully before proceeding.

Arma 3 runs its 64-bit executable by default. The 32-bit version is deprecated since update 2.20 and the launcher no longer offers it as an option. No special configuration is needed. The current versions of the game, ACRE2, and TFAR are all 64-bit.

Once the download is complete, launch Arma 3 from Steam. Wait for the game to reach the main menu. You do not need to enter any mission or server. Reaching the main menu is enough.

This first launch is essential. Proton generates the Wine prefix for Arma 3 during this step. The Wine prefix must exist before TeamSpeak 3 can be installed into it. If you skip this step, subsequent steps will fail.

Once the main menu appears, exit the game normally.

## Installing the Arma 3 Unix Launcher (Recommended)

The official Bohemia Interactive launcher does not integrate well with Linux mod management. The **Arma 3 Unix Launcher** by muttleyxd is a purpose-built replacement. It is strongly recommended.

The Unix Launcher provides the following advantages over the official launcher:

- Native Linux interface with no compatibility issues.
- Reliable mod management and preset loading.
- Direct support for launch parameters.
- No requirement for the `-nolauncher` flag.

Install the Arma 3 Unix Launcher from one of the following sources:

- **Arch Linux AUR**: `yay -S arma3-unix-launcher-bin`
- **.deb or .AppImage**: [Download from GitHub](https://github.com/muttleyxd/arma3-unix-launcher/releases/latest)

To open a mod preset, right-click on the mod list in the Unix Launcher. You can disable all mods from the right-click menu before loading a different preset.

\newpage

# Chapter 5 – The Arma3Helper Script

## What the Script Does

The Arma3Helper script is a command-line tool that manages the interface between Linux and Arma 3's Wine prefix. Its main functions are:

- Launches TeamSpeak 3 inside the correct Wine environment.
- Installs TeamSpeak 3 into Arma's Wine prefix.
- Runs winetricks and winecfg inside the Arma prefix.
- Provides diagnostic and dependency-checking tools.

The script also applies several automatic protections at every launch:

- **Setup wizard**: On first use, walks through the full setup: dependency check, TeamSpeak 3 install if missing, Winetricks DLLs, and radio plugin verification.
- **Prefix protection**: Warns if the configured Proton version differs from the version that created the prefix. Changing Proton versions can break audio and plugins.
- **Gamepad plugin removal**: Deletes the crashing Gamepad and Joystick Hotkey Support plugin from the prefix (Chapter 7).
- **S: drive preservation**: Exports the variables Proton needs so the game's `S:` drive survives (Chapter 5, "Steam Compatibility Paths").
- **Plugin verification**: Warns with the exact fix when a radio plugin is missing or disabled.
- **Single-instance guard**: Refuses a second launch while one instance is already running, to protect the prefix.

The script is required for ACRE2 and TFAR. Without it, TeamSpeak 3 will not communicate with Arma 3.

## Obtaining the Script

Download the script from the GitHub repository:

``` bash
# Download directly to your home directory:
curl -o ~/Arma3Helper.sh \
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UKSFTA/UKSFTA-AOL/master/Arma3Helper.sh

# Make it executable:
chmod +x ~/Arma3Helper.sh
```

Place the script in your home directory for easy access. All commands in this guide assume it is located there.

## Configuring the Script

The script can be configured in two ways. The preferred method is an external configuration file, which persists across script updates. The alternative is to edit the script directly, but this is overwritten whenever you run the update command.

Create the external configuration file with:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh createconfig
```

This creates a file at `~/.config/arma3helper/config`. Open it in a text editor and adjust the values as described below.

### Setting the Proton Version

In most cases you do not need to set the Proton version at all. Arma3Helper reads the version file inside Arma's prefix and matches it to an installed Proton build automatically. This covers official, GE-Proton, and other custom builds.

Set `PROTON_OFFICIAL_VERSION` manually only if auto-detection fails, or if you want to force a specific official version. The value must match the version selected in Steam exactly.

``` bash
# Official Proton example:
PROTON_OFFICIAL_VERSION="10.0"

# Proton Experimental:
PROTON_OFFICIAL_VERSION="Experimental"
```

If you are using a custom Proton build such as GE-Proton, leave `PROTON_OFFICIAL_VERSION` empty and set `PROTON_CUSTOM_VERSION` instead:

``` bash
PROTON_CUSTOM_VERSION="GE-Proton9-20"
```

To find the exact name of your installed custom build, run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh listproton
```

### Steam Library Paths (usually not needed)

The script automatically detects all Steam library paths by reading Steam's configuration file. This includes external drives and secondary libraries. In most cases, you do not need to set `COMPAT_DATA_PATH` or `STEAM_LIBRARY_PATH` manually.

If auto-detection fails, the debug command will show what the script found:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh debug
```

Set paths manually only if the debug output shows an incorrect location.

### Esync and Fsync

Esync and Fsync are performance features that reduce CPU overhead. They must match the settings Arma 3 uses in Steam. If you have not explicitly disabled either for Arma 3, leave both as `true` in the config file.

``` bash
ESYNC=true
FSYNC=true
```

### Steam Compatibility Paths (normally automatic)

Some Proton builds enable the `gamedrive` option (Proton Hotfix does by default). These builds need `STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH` and `STEAM_COMPAT_LIBRARY_PATHS` to find the game's Steam library. Without them, Proton deletes the `S:` drive from the prefix, and Arma 3 fails server signature checks with kicks such as:

```
Files "dta\bin.pbo" are not signed by a key accepted by this server.
```

The script derives both variables from `COMPAT_DATA_PATH` automatically, so you do not normally need to set them. Set them in the config file only to override the derived values.

``` bash
STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH=""
STEAM_COMPAT_LIBRARY_PATHS=""
```

## Checking Dependencies

After configuring the script, run the dependency check:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps
```

The check reports the status of all required packages. If any are missing, it prints the exact install command to use. Resolve all missing packages before continuing.

The check also verifies that the **Proton BattlEye Runtime** is installed in one of your Steam libraries. BattlEye-protected servers require this component for the client. If it is missing, install it from Steam's **Library → Tools** list. The check additionally warns if your Steam library sits on a drive mounted with `noexec`, which prevents Proton and mods from running there.

## Available Script Commands

The following commands are available. Run `./Arma3Helper.sh help` to see this list at any time.

- **`./Arma3Helper.sh`**: Launch TeamSpeak 3 (start Arma first)
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh install <exe>`**: Install TeamSpeak 3 into the prefix
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks Arma`**: Install recommended DLLs
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks <args>`**: Run any winetricks command
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh winecfg`**: Open Wine configuration
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps`**: Check required packages
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh listproton`**: List available Proton versions
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh debug`**: Print diagnostic information
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh update`**: Update script from GitHub (keeps a backup at `Arma3Helper.sh.bak-arma3helper`)
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh createconfig`**: Create external config file
- **`./Arma3Helper.sh help`**: Show usage information

# Chapter 6 – Installing Required Windows Components

Before installing TeamSpeak 3, install the Windows components that Arma 3 and its radio plugins require. The script handles this with a single command.

Launch Arma 3 at least once (see Chapter 4, 'Downloading and First Launch') before running this command. The Wine prefix must exist.

Run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks Arma
```

This installs the following components into Arma's Wine prefix:

- **`d3dcompiler_43`**: DirectX shader compiler. Fixes certain rendering issues.
- **`d3dx10_43`**: DirectX 10 runtime. Required by some mods.
- **`d3dx11_43`**: DirectX 11 runtime. Required by some mods.
- **`mfc140`**: Microsoft C++ runtime. Required by some mods.
- **`xact_x64`**: Microsoft XACT audio engine. Fixes audio problems.
- **`xaudio29`**: XAudio2 library. Fixes audio crackling at high volume.
- **`xaudio2_9`**: XAudio 2.9 library. Fixes audio crackling after the Arma 2.22 update.

The installation may take several minutes. Do not interrupt it. A slow internet connection will extend the time needed.

After completion, launch Arma 3 once to verify the game works correctly. Check that audio functions as expected. If thermal vision effects are broken in-game, this step resolves that as well.

\newpage

# Chapter 7 – Installing TeamSpeak 3

## Why TeamSpeak 3 Must Run Inside Wine

ACRE2 and TFAR communicate between Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 using shared memory. Both applications must run inside the same Wine environment for this to work. The Windows version of TeamSpeak 3 must therefore be installed directly into Arma's Wine prefix.

The native Linux TeamSpeak 3 client cannot load the ACRE2 or TFAR Windows plugins. Do not use it for this purpose.

## Downloading TeamSpeak 3

The script downloads and verifies the latest TeamSpeak 3 Windows installer for you. Run the install command with no arguments:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh install
```

The script:

1.  Queries TeamSpeak's official version endpoint for the latest Windows x64 client.
2.  Downloads the installer.
3.  Verifies its SHA-256 checksum against the published value.
4.  Runs the installer silently with the **Install for All Users** option.

If the download server blocks the automated request, the script prints the manual download URL. In that case, download the **Windows 64-bit** installer from the [official website](https://www.teamspeak.com/en/downloads/#ts3client) and pass its path instead:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh install ~/Downloads/TeamSpeak3-Client-win64-3.x.x.exe
```

Do not use the Linux version. Do not use TeamSpeak 5. TeamSpeak 5 does not yet support the ACRE2 or TFAR plugins.

## Running the Installer

The silent installer places TeamSpeak 3 at `C:\Program Files\TeamSpeak 3 Client\` inside the prefix, which is the location the script expects.

For a manual install through the Wine window instead, run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh install /path/to/TeamSpeak3-Client-win64-3.x.x.exe
```

The installer opens in a Wine window. Follow these three critical steps. Failing to follow them exactly will cause the script to be unable to find TeamSpeak 3 afterwards.

### Critical Step 1 – Select 'Install for All Users'

When the installer asks where to install TeamSpeak 3, select the option labelled **Install for All Users**. Do not select **Install for current user only**.

The reason for this is important. 'Install for All Users' places TeamSpeak 3 at:

```
C:\Program Files\TeamSpeak 3 Client\
```

'Install for current user only' places it at:

```
C:\Users\steamuser\AppData\Local\TeamSpeak 3 Client\
```

The Arma3Helper script looks for TeamSpeak 3 in `Program Files`. If it is installed to `AppData` instead, the script will not find it.

### Critical Step 2 – Accept the Default Installation Path

Do not change the installation path. Accept it exactly as the installer presents it. The default path will read:

```
C:\Program Files\TeamSpeak 3 Client
```

Leave this unchanged and click **Next** or **Install**.

### Critical Step 3 – Complete the Installation

Proceed through any remaining installer screens and allow the installation to complete. You do not need to launch TeamSpeak 3 from the installer at the end.

## Verifying the Installation

Verify that TeamSpeak 3 was installed correctly by attempting to launch it. First start Arma 3 from Steam, wait for it to reach the main menu, then run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh
```

The launch checks run automatically:

- If TeamSpeak 3 is missing, the script offers to download and install it.
- If a radio plugin is missing or was disabled after a crash, the script prints the exact command to fix it.
- If Arma 3 is not running, the script warns that the radio plugins cannot connect.

TeamSpeak 3 should open. If it does not, run the debug command and check that the TS3 executable path is correct:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh debug
```

Look for the line labelled **TS3 executable found**. If it reads `NO`, TeamSpeak 3 was not installed to the expected path. The most common cause is selecting "Install for current user only" instead of "Install for All Users" during installation.

If the installer hangs at the message `fsync: up and running`, you are likely using Proton Experimental. Switch Arma 3 to a stable Proton version in Steam (Chapter 3), then run the install command again.

## Configuring TeamSpeak 3 After Installation

Once TeamSpeak 3 is running, set the following options before connecting to any server.

### Gamepad and Joystick Plugin

A built-in TeamSpeak 3 plugin called **Gamepad and Joystick Hotkey Support** causes TeamSpeak 3 to crash when a gamepad or joystick is connected. TeamSpeak has not fixed this bug. The plugin is deleted automatically every time you launch TeamSpeak 3 with Arma3Helper, so no manual action is needed.

If you experience crashes after a few seconds of TeamSpeak 3 running, this plugin was almost certainly the cause. If you run TeamSpeak 3 through Steam directly instead of through Arma3Helper, delete these files from the prefix's plugins folder:

``` bash
rm -rf "$COMPAT_DATA_PATH/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/Roaming/TS3Client/plugins/gamepad_joystick"*
```

Bluetooth controllers also trigger the crash – for example, a paired Stadia controller will crash TeamSpeak 3 even when it is not in use.

\newpage

# Chapter 8 – ACRE2 Configuration

## Overview

ACRE2 provides the most realistic radio simulation available for Arma 3. It models individual radio types with accurate transmission properties. This chapter covers installation and verification of the ACRE2 plugin.

## Required Mods

ACRE2 requires the following mods to be active:

- **CBA_A3** (Workshop ID: 450814997): Community Base Addons. Required by most Arma mods.
- **ACRE2** (Workshop ID: 751965892): The radio simulation mod itself.

Subscribe to both mods in the Steam Workshop or through the Arma 3 Unix Launcher. Make sure they are enabled in your mod list before launching.

## How ACRE2 Installs Its Plugin

ACRE2 attempts to install its TeamSpeak plugin automatically. When you launch Arma 3 with ACRE2 active, the mod detects the TeamSpeak 3 installation inside the Wine prefix and copies the plugin files there.

A pop-up window will appear on the first run confirming the installation. If the pop-up does not appear, or if TeamSpeak 3 cannot load the plugin, the manual installation described below may be attempted as a last resort.

## Manual Plugin Installation (When Auto-Install Fails)

::: {.callout-warning}
Manual installation should only be attempted if the automatic process fails. Incorrectly placing files can cause plugin conflicts.
:::

Run the repair command:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh acremod
```

The script locates the ACRE2 mod folder in your Steam library and copies the plugin DLLs into the prefix TeamSpeak install. The command is safe to re-run; it overwrites the plugin with the current mod version.

## Troubleshooting the Radio Connection

If ACRE2 or TFAR reports that it "cannot find the game instance", run the connection diagnostic:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh acrecheck
```

The check names the exact cause in order:

1.  **Arma 3 is not running.** Start Arma 3 from Steam, wait for the main menu, then start TeamSpeak 3.
2.  **The radio mod is not in the loaded mod list.** Enable ACRE2 (and TFAR if your unit uses it) in your mod launcher.

The script also lists loaded and installed mods for debugging:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh listmods        # both lists
./Arma3Helper.sh listmods loaded # only the current/last session
```

The loaded list is read from the running Arma 3 process, so it always reflects the current session. It flags ACRE2 and TFAR presence so you can see at a glance whether the radio mod is actually active.

## Verifying the Full Radio Chain

To verify everything at once, run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh verifyradio
```

The check works down a three-stage chain for each radio mod:

1.  **Workshop mod downloaded** : the mod folder exists in a Steam library.
2.  **Mod loaded in the game** : the mod is in the current session's loaded mod list.
3.  **TeamSpeak plugin installed** : the plugin DLL is in the prefix TeamSpeak install.

Each failing stage prints the exact fix. For example, a plugin disabled after a crash reports:

```
[FAIL] TeamSpeak plugin disabled after a crash
  Re-enable with:  ./Arma3Helper.sh tfarmod --enable
```

Run `verifyradio` after any change to confirm the whole chain is healthy before joining a mission.

## Mods on an External Drive

If the game or its Workshop mods sit on an external drive, two mount problems can break loading:

- **`noexec` mount**: Proton and Workshop mods cannot run from a drive mounted with `noexec`. Check with `cat /proc/mounts | grep noexec`. Remount with exec: `sudo mount -o remount,exec <mountpoint>`, or move the Steam library to an ext4 drive.

Run `./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps` to check for the `noexec` mount problem.

## Verifying ACRE2

Follow this sequence to verify ACRE2 is working:

1.  Start TeamSpeak 3 using `./Arma3Helper.sh` and connect to a server.
2.  Launch Arma 3 with CBA_A3 and ACRE2 active.
3.  Wait for the main menu to load. Arma will attempt plugin installation.
4.  Switch back to TeamSpeak 3. Go to **Tools** → **Options** → **Addons**.
5.  Confirm the ACRE2 plugin is listed and enabled.

::: {.callout-important}
Plugins are typically enabled by default. If you see the plugin is already enabled, do **not** click 'Enable', as this will toggle it off. If the plugin is not working, verify it is truly enabled in this menu.
:::


If the plugin is listed but not working, verify that both Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 are running under the same user account. They should not be run with different permission levels (for example, one as root and one as a normal user).

## ACRE2 In-Game Settings

ACRE2 settings are accessible in-game through the CBA Settings System. Press **Escape** and navigate to **Configure** → **Addon Options** → **ACRE2**. Common settings include:

- **Radio Volume**: Controls the in-ear radio volume.
- **Speaker Volume**: Volume of radio traffic from players physically nearby.
- **Babel Languages**: Mission makers can configure these.

\newpage

# Chapter 9 – TFAR Configuration

## Overview

TFAR simulates military radio communication through TeamSpeak 3. Unlike ACRE2, TFAR does not install its plugin automatically. The Arma3Helper script copies the plugin into the prefix TeamSpeak install with a single command.

## Required Mods

TFAR requires the following mod:

- **Task Force Arrowhead Radio (BETA!!!)** (Workshop ID: 894678801): The main TFAR mod.

Some communities use an older version of TFAR (Workshop ID: 620019431). Check with your unit which version they use before subscribing.

TFAR does not require CBA_A3 in all versions, but most TFAR-using communities run CBA_A3 alongside it. Confirm with your unit.

## Installing the TFAR Plugin

Subscribe to the TFAR mod in the Steam Workshop and let it download. The script finds the plugin inside the Workshop mod folder.

Run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh tfarmod
```

The script:

1.  Locates the TFAR plugin in the Workshop mod folder.
2.  Extracts it if it is packaged as a `.ts3plugin` archive.
3.  Copies the DLL files and the `radio-sounds` folder into the prefix TeamSpeak plugins directory.

The command is safe to re-run. It overwrites the plugin files with the current mod version.

If the script reports "Could not find the TFAR plugin", the mod is not installed or not downloaded. Subscribe to it in Steam, let the download finish, then run the command again.

## Enabling the TFAR Plugin

Launch TeamSpeak 3 using the Arma3Helper script:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh
```

In TeamSpeak 3, go to **Tools** → **Options** → **Addons** (or **Plugins**). You should see the TFAR plugin listed.

::: {.callout-important}
Plugins are typically enabled by default. If you see the plugin is already enabled, do **not** click 'Enable', as this will toggle it off. If the plugin is not working, verify it is truly enabled in this menu.
:::

## Plugin Disabled After a Crash

If the TFAR plugin ever crashes TeamSpeak 3, TeamSpeak renames its DLL to `TFAR_win64.dll.disabled` so it is not loaded again. This is TeamSpeak's crash protection, not a TFAR fault.

Re-enable the plugin with:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh tfarmod --enable
```

The script also reports a disabled plugin during `checkdeps`, so you will see the problem before it bites.

## Verifying TFAR

Run the dependency check and confirm both radio plugins are present:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps
```

The output shows the ACRE2 and TFAR plugin status. Then verify in game:

1.  Start TeamSpeak 3 using `./Arma3Helper.sh` and connect to a server.
2.  Confirm the TFAR plugin shows as active in TeamSpeak.
3.  Launch Arma 3 with the TFAR mod active.
4.  Load into a mission. The TFAR status indicator should appear.
5.  Open the radio shortwave interface with the default keybind.

You should hear radio traffic through TeamSpeak once TFAR connects. If you can hear others but they cannot hear you, check your microphone settings in TeamSpeak and your push-to-talk keybinding.

## TFAR-Specific Notes

TFAR works differently on dedicated servers. The server must also run the TFAR server plugin. Contact your server administrator if in-game radios appear to work but no audio is transmitted.

TFAR's frequency management is handled through the in-game radio interface. Consult your community's standard operating procedures for frequency assignment.

\newpage

# Chapter 10 – Troubleshooting

## Audio Problems

### No Sound or Distorted Audio

If Arma 3 has no sound or distorted audio, make sure GStreamer and its 32-bit equivalents are installed (Chapter 2). Then run:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks Arma
```

This installs the XACT and XAudio2 components that Arma 3 requires.

### Audio Crackling at High Volumes

The Arma 2.22 update moved the game to XAudio 2.9. Some Proton versions crackle with it. The `winetricks Arma` command (Chapter 6) installs `xaudio2_9`, which resolves this.

If crackling persists, add an override for `xaudio2_9` instead of `xaudio2_7`:

```
WINEDLLOVERRIDES="xaudio2_9=n" %command%
```

Alternatively set it through winecfg:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh winecfg
```

Navigate to the **Libraries** tab and add `xaudio2_9` with the override set to **Native**.

If crackling persists after the DLL fix, set the audio sample rate to 44.1 kHz in your desktop audio settings. This is a reported workaround for the XAudio 2.9 regression. You can also roll Arma 3 back to update 2.20 while Bohemia investigates, but the DLL fix resolves it for most users.

## Arma 3 Crashes on Startup

A crash immediately after launch, before the main menu appears, usually indicates missing Vulkan support. Install the appropriate package (Chapter 2, 'Resolving Startup Crashes').

After installing, verify Vulkan is working:

``` bash
vulkaninfo 2>&1 | head -20
```

If `vulkaninfo` reports errors about a missing GPU or driver, your graphics driver may need updating.

## TeamSpeak 3 Crashes After a Few Seconds

This is almost always caused by the Gamepad and Joystick Hotkey Support plugin. Arma3Helper deletes the plugin automatically at every launch, so this should not happen when TeamSpeak 3 is started through the script.

The crash occurs specifically when a controller, joystick, or other HID device is connected. Wireless controllers count too: a Bluetooth controller such as a Stadia controller triggers the crash even when it is not in use. Unplugging or unpairing the device temporarily will also stop the crash, but deleting the plugin files is the correct solution (see Chapter 7, "Gamepad and Joystick Plugin").

## ACRE2 Plugin Not Found by TeamSpeak

If TeamSpeak 3 cannot load the ACRE2 plugin, check the following:

- Arma 3 was launched with ACRE2 and CBA_A3 active.
- Both Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 are running as the same user.
- The plugin files exist in the TeamSpeak plugins directory (Chapter 8).

Run the manual plugin installation described in Chapter 8 if the automatic process has failed.

## TFAR Plugin Missing from TeamSpeak

If the TFAR plugin does not appear in TeamSpeak 3 after copying the files, verify the following:

- Both `TFAR_win32.dll` and `TFAR_win64.dll` are present in the plugins folder.
- The `radio-sounds` folder is also present.
- The path used was correct. Run `./Arma3Helper.sh debug` to confirm the COMPAT_DATA_PATH.

Check that file permissions allow reading:

``` bash
ls -la "$HOME/.steam/steam/steamapps/compatdata/107410/pfx/drive_c/Program Files/TeamSpeak 3 Client/plugins/"
```

## ACRE2 and TeamSpeak Are Not Connecting

The message 'ACRE is not connected to TeamSpeak' appears in-game when Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 cannot communicate. There are two known causes.

### Cause 1 – TeamSpeak Not Sharing Arma's Wine Environment

Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 must share the same Wine prefix. Always use the Arma3Helper script to launch TeamSpeak 3. Never launch it independently.

The correct sequence is:

1.  Launch Arma 3 from Steam.
2.  Wait for Arma 3 to reach the main menu.
3.  Run `./Arma3Helper.sh` in a terminal.
4.  Wait for TeamSpeak 3 to open.
5.  Connect to the TeamSpeak server.
6.  Load into the mission.

### Cause 2 – Wrong Wine Server (Rare)

ACRE2's named pipes are Wine server objects. Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3 must attach to the same Wine server. This happens automatically when both run against the same prefix, because the Wine server socket lives in `/tmp/.wine-<uid>/` and Steam Linux Runtime shares `/tmp` and `/home` with the container by default.

If you see `Pipe error: Read CreateFileA WinErrCode: 2` in Arma's `.rpt` log every 16 seconds, the two applications are on different Wine servers. This is not a launch-option problem. The usual causes are:

- TeamSpeak 3 was launched from outside the script (for example, a native Linux TeamSpeak or a Windows TeamSpeak started with the wrong prefix). Always start TeamSpeak 3 with `./Arma3Helper.sh`.
- The prefix was reset or moved while both applications were running. Restart Arma 3 and TeamSpeak 3.
- Arma 3 is running but TeamSpeak 3 never started. Both must be up at the same time.

No Steam launch options are needed. The script does not modify Arma's launch options.

## Script Cannot Find TeamSpeak 3

If the script reports that TeamSpeak 3 is not found, run the debug command and check the reported path:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh debug
```

The debug output shows the expected TeamSpeak 3 path. Verify the file exists at that location:

``` bash
ls -la "/path/shown/in/debug/output/ts3client_win64.exe"
```

If the file is in `AppData` rather than `Program Files`, TeamSpeak 3 was installed as "current user only". Uninstall it and repeat the installation process (Chapter 7), selecting "Install for All Users".

## Proton-Specific Issues

The following problems come from ProtonDB reports for Arma 3. Each is uncommon but appears across multiple user reports.

### Game Freezes on Fast Mouse Movement

High-polling-rate mice (8000 Hz) can freeze the game during fast movement. Set this launch option:

```
PROTON_USE_RAW_INPUT=1 %command%
```

Alternatively, lower the mouse polling rate to 1000 Hz in its configuration software.

### Game Runs at 640×480 Resolution

Some Proton versions lock Arma 3 to 640×480 on certain GPUs. Update to Proton 9.0-4 or newer, then restart the game.

### Mouse Cursor Escapes the Game Window

On multi-monitor setups the cursor can leave the game window and land on another screen. Use windowed fullscreen mode, or set these options in `winecfg` (Chapter 6):

- **Automatically capture the mouse in full screen windows**

### Cursor Jumps or Delays on AMD GPUs

Latest Mesa releases can cause cursor problems under some compositors. Disable the compositor for the game session, or run Arma 3 inside gamescope:

``` bash
gamescope -f -- %command%
```

### VRAM Usage Grows Over Time

Some users report a memory leak that fills VRAM after several hours of play. Restart Arma 3 when frame rate drops. There is no known fix as of this writing.

## Getting Further Help

If this troubleshooting chapter does not resolve your problem, gather diagnostic information and ask for help on the ArmaOnUnix Discord:

``` bash
./Arma3Helper.sh debug
./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps
```

Copy the output of both commands and include it when asking for help. This information allows others to diagnose the problem quickly.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do **not** open a GitHub issue before asking on the Discord. Most problems are configuration issues that the community can resolve rapidly. GitHub issues are reserved for confirmed bugs. Note, this discord is not run by the script author but by volunteers from the community. Be patient and respectful when asking for help, this also is not related to UKSF Taskforce Alpha in any way.
:::

[Discord: https://discord.gg/p28Ra36](https://discord.gg/p28Ra36)

\newpage

# Chapter 11 – Performance Optimisation

## Recommended Launch Parameters

Arma 3 supports a range of launch parameters that improve startup time and frame rate. Add them in Arma 3's Steam **Launch Options** field (Chapter 3, 'Adding Arma 3 Launch Options') or in the Arma 3 Unix Launcher.

The following baseline is safe for all systems and is what the current Linux guides recommend:

```
%command% -noLauncher -noSplash -skipIntro -world=empty -noLogs
```

- **`-noLauncher`**: Skips the Arma 3 launcher, which is slow and can glitch under Proton. Use the Arma 3 Unix Launcher for mod management instead.
- **`-noSplash`**: Skips opening splash screens. Reduces startup time.
- **`-skipIntro`**: Shows a static main menu background. Minor startup speedup.
- **`-world=empty`**: Loads an empty world for the main menu. Significant startup speedup.
- **`-noLogs`**: Disables log writing. Slight performance gain. Remove this when troubleshooting.

Do not use the old CPU-tuning parameters. Since update 2.20 the engine configures its own thread count and CPU affinity. Manual overrides such as `-cpuCount`, `-exThreads`, and `-enableHT` now reduce performance on most systems. Bohemia Interactive states this directly in the 2.20 performance optimisation report. Leave thread settings alone.

The parameter `-cpuCount=1` is sometimes recommended for fixing certain crashes, but it significantly reduces performance. Try it only if other solutions have failed.

Do not use `-malloc` parameters. The old `tbb4malloc_bi` recommendation is outdated and the game allocates memory correctly by default. Custom allocators such as `mimalloc` are verified on Windows only. Their benefit under Proton is unproven, and BattlEye may block them.

## Proton-Specific Settings

### Mission Start Freezes

If Arma 3 freezes when a mission starts, disable Esync for the game. This applies to Proton 10 and older. Proton 11 obsoleted the variable.

```
PROTON_NO_ESYNC=1 %command%
```

### Variables That Do Nothing on Current Proton

- **`PROTON_ENABLE_NVAPI`**: This was a Proton-GE-era variable. Current Proton enables NVAPI by default. Setting it does nothing.
- **`PROTON_FSR`**: This was a Proton 6.x-era variable. It was replaced by `WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR`. Setting it does nothing.
- **`WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR`**: This is a Proton-GE feature only. It does nothing on official Proton builds.

### Measuring Performance

**`DXVK_HUD`** draws an in-game overlay with frame rate, frame time, and GPU information. Use it to measure the effect of any change, then remove it.

```
DXVK_HUD=fps %command%
```

## General Linux Gaming Optimisations

The following are not Arma-specific but apply broadly to Linux gaming.

### Kernel Scheduling

A custom kernel can provide meaningful performance improvements. The `linux-tkg` project on GitHub offers kernel builds optimised for gaming. This is an advanced option. Research it before attempting it.

### GameMode

**GameMode** (by Feral Interactive) automatically applies performance tweaks when a game runs. It adjusts CPU governor, process scheduling, and other settings. Install it from your package manager:

``` bash
# Arch Linux:
sudo pacman -S gamemode

# Debian/Ubuntu:
sudo apt install gamemode

# Fedora:
sudo dnf install gamemode
```

Enable it by adding `gamemoderun %command%` to Arma 3's Steam launch options.

### MangoHud

**MangoHud** provides an in-game performance overlay for Linux. It displays frame rate, frame time, CPU and GPU usage, and temperatures. It is useful for measuring the effect of any optimisation changes.

``` bash
# Arch Linux:
sudo pacman -S mangohud

# Debian/Ubuntu:
sudo apt install mangohud

# Fedora:
sudo dnf install mangohud
```

Enable it by adding `MANGOHUD=1 %command%` to the Steam launch options.

\newpage

# Annex A – Glossary

- **ACRE2**: Advanced Combat Radio Environment 2. An Arma 3 mod simulating military radio communications.
- **AppData**: A Windows user-specific folder for application data. Located at `C:\Users\<name>\AppData\`.
- **CBA_A3**: Community Base Addons for Arma 3. A library of functions and systems used by many mods.
- **compatdata**: The directory containing a game's Wine prefix. Named after 'compatibility data'.
- **Esync/Fsync**: Optimisations that reduce CPU overhead in Wine by replacing kernel synchronisation primitives with user-space equivalents.
- **GE-Proton**: Glorious Eggroll Proton. A community-maintained Proton build with additional patches.
- **GStreamer**: An open-source multimedia framework. Arma 3 uses it for audio.
- **Proton**: Valve's compatibility layer for running Windows games on Linux.
- **protontricks**: A wrapper around winetricks that automatically sets the correct Wine prefix for a Steam game.
- **Steam App ID**: A unique number identifying a game on Steam. Arma 3's App ID is 107410.
- **TFAR**: Task Force Arrowhead Radio. An Arma 3 mod providing radio simulation via TeamSpeak 3.
- **Wine**: An open-source compatibility layer that translates Windows API calls to Linux.
- **Wine prefix**: An isolated Windows environment created by Wine. Each game typically has its own prefix.
- **winetricks**: A script that automates the installation of Windows components into a Wine prefix.
- **Workshop ID**: A unique number identifying a mod on the Steam Workshop.

\newpage

# Annex B – Quick Reference Commands

## First-Time Setup (in order)

``` bash
# 1. Download the script
curl -o ~/Arma3Helper.sh \
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UKSFTA/UKSFTA-AOL/master/Arma3Helper.sh
chmod +x ~/Arma3Helper.sh

# 2. Create the config file (auto-detection works out of the box)
./Arma3Helper.sh createconfig

# 3. Check dependencies
./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps

# 4. Install TeamSpeak 3 (downloads and installs the latest version)
./Arma3Helper.sh install

# 5. Install Windows components (after first Arma launch)
./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks Arma

# 6. Point Arma's Documents and Downloads at your real host folders
./Arma3Helper.sh bindhost

# 7. Verify the radio mods are fully installed and loaded
./Arma3Helper.sh verifyradio
```

## Daily Usage

``` bash
# Start Arma 3 from Steam, wait for main menu, then:
./Arma3Helper.sh
```

## Radio Plugin Commands

``` bash
# Install the ACRE2 plugin manually (if auto-install failed):
./Arma3Helper.sh acremod

# Install the TFAR plugin (TFAR does not auto-install):
./Arma3Helper.sh tfarmod

# Re-enable a plugin TeamSpeak disabled after a crash:
./Arma3Helper.sh tfarmod --enable

# Diagnose why radios cannot find the game instance:
./Arma3Helper.sh acrecheck

# Full radio chain check (mod downloaded, loaded, plugin installed):
./Arma3Helper.sh verifyradio

# List installed and loaded mods:
./Arma3Helper.sh listmods
```

## Prefix Management

``` bash
# Diagnose the prefix (read-only):
./Arma3Helper.sh prefix doctor

# Repair the prefix in place:
./Arma3Helper.sh prefix reset

# Recreate the prefix (backs up user data first):
./Arma3Helper.sh prefix reset --full
```

## Troubleshooting Commands

``` bash
# Full diagnostic output (share this when asking for help):
./Arma3Helper.sh debug

# Dependency check:
./Arma3Helper.sh checkdeps

# List Proton versions:
./Arma3Helper.sh listproton

# Install recommended audio/visual DLLs:
./Arma3Helper.sh winetricks Arma

# Open Wine config:
./Arma3Helper.sh winecfg
```
